## Kitchen Leak Response Plan for a Chicago Rental

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg

You have a **slow under-sink leak**, **minor cabinet swelling**, and **5 days without a landlord response**. The safest approach is to document clearly, give a firm written repair request, and reduce any risk of further damage while keeping everything professional.

## Practical Checklist and 72-Hour Repair Request

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check2-square.svg

| Step | What to do | What to keep |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Take dated photos and a short video of the leak, cabinet swelling, and any pooled water | Files with timestamps; wide shot + close-up |
| 2 | Note the date you first saw it and each time you observed it | A simple timeline with dates and times |
| 3 | Save every message to the landlord or property manager | Texts, emails, portal screenshots, call logs |
| 4 | Send one clear written repair request | Keep a copy of the exact message sent |
| 5 | Reduce further damage | Place a bucket/towel, stop using the sink if needed, and move items away from the cabinet |
| 6 | Check for safety concerns | Look for mold smell, electrical outlets nearby, or worsening water spread |
| 7 | Follow up in writing if there is no reply | Keep the follow-up short and factual |
| 8 | Escalate through building management or maintenance contact if available | Names, dates, and response records |

### What to include in your documentation
- The exact location: **kitchen sink cabinet, under-sink area**
- The issue: **slow leak**
- Visible damage: **minor cabinet swelling**
- Impact: whether you had to stop using the sink or move stored items
- Date noticed: **2026-03-18**
- Landlord nonresponse: **5 days without reply**

### How to communicate
- Use **written communication first** so there is a record.
- Keep the tone **calm, factual, and firm**.
- Ask for **repair within 72 hours** and request a reply confirming next steps.
- If you already called, follow up by email or portal message so the request is documented.

### Simple protection steps
- Do not ignore the leak, even if it seems small.
- Keep the area dry as much as possible to limit cabinet damage.
- If the leak worsens, shut off the under-sink water valves if you know how and it is safe to do so.
- Avoid making permanent repairs yourself unless you are certain it is allowed and safe.
- Keep receipts if you buy towels, buckets, or other basic items to control damage.

## Neutral 72-Hour Repair Email Template

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg

**Subject:** Request for Repair: Slow Leak Under Kitchen Sink

Hello [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I am writing to report a slow leak under the kitchen sink in my apartment. I first noticed the issue on **2026-03-18**. The leak has already caused **minor cabinet swelling**.

I previously reported this issue and have not received a response after **5 days**. Please arrange for inspection and repair **within 72 hours** of this email. If possible, please reply to confirm when maintenance will be scheduled.

For reference, the apartment is a **2-bedroom unit, approximately 850 square feet**, located in Chicago, Illinois.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Apartment Number]
[Phone Number]
[Email Address]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Save Evidence] https://www.google.com/drive/
Action: [Button: Send Email] https://mail.google.com/
Action: [Button: Follow Up Log] https://docs.google.com/

## Sources

- General tenant repair guidance: https://www.consumer.ftc.gov/
- Home maintenance leak basics: https://www.energy.gov/
- Documenting property damage tips: https://www.ready.gov/kit
